title: Eiffel Tower
text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It was designed by the engineer Gustave Eiffel and completed in 1889 as the entrance arch to the 1889 World's Fair.

title: Mount Everest
text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. Its elevation was most recently measured at 8,848.86 metres.

title: Water boiling point
text: At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius, which is equivalent to 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

title: Python programming language
text: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It emphasizes code readability.

title: Great Wall of China
text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of China, with major construction occurring during the Ming dynasty.

title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesize nutrients from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen as a byproduct.

title: Amazon River
text: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river by discharge volume of water in the world, and by some measurements the longest.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
text: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance who painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, and made pioneering studies in anatomy and engineering.

title: Speed of light
text: The speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second, a universal physical constant denoted by the symbol c.

title: United Nations founding
text: The United Nations was founded on 24 October 1945 after World War II, with the goal of maintaining international peace and security.

title: DNA structure
text: The double helix structure of DNA was described by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953, building on X-ray diffraction data from Rosalind Franklin.

title: Sahara Desert
text: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of North Africa, with an area comparable to that of the United States or China.
